title: 3 in 4 Maryland voters oppose new data centers, UMBC poll finds
key_facts: A University of Maryland, Baltimore County (UMBC) poll of likely voters found 78% oppose new data centres being built in Maryland and 13% support them; 370 likely voters were asked this question.
A separate group of 406 voters was asked about a new data centre near their community: 77% opposed and 16% supported.
80% of likely voters expect new data centres to have a mostly negative impact on household electricity costs; 6% expect a mostly positive impact.
75% expect a mostly negative impact on quality of life for people near data centre sites; 68% expect a negative impact on water quality and 60% on air quality.
49% expect a mostly negative impact on Maryland's economy, against 19% who expect a positive one; on jobs, 37% expect a negative impact and 26% a positive one.
67% of likely voters say they believe AI will have a negative impact on society.
quote_evidence: Among 370 likely voters asked about new data centers being built in Maryland, 78% opposed them and 13% supported them.
Just 6% of those surveyed said new data centers would have a mostly positive impact on electric costs.
Seventy-five percent expect a negative impact on the quality of life for people living near data center sites.
why_it_matters_hint: Most Maryland likely voters oppose new data centres, mainly over electricity bills; the poll is one survey.
